synthesis.description: An organiser, often a manager or assistant, announces a group, staff or management meeting or asks recipients to hold a date, and asks them to reply if they cannot attend or which of several dates suits them. Attendees confirm or sign up, the organiser collects head counts for catering, books a conference room or sends a calendar invitation, and sometimes chases more detail about the meeting from whoever requested it.
steps: Someone requests a meeting or the organiser plans a regular group meeting.
The organiser emails the date, time and room, or asks recipients to hold or choose between dates.
Recipients reply with availability or sign up for a date.
The organiser tallies attendance and finalises numbers for food or space.
The organiser books the room or sends a calendar invitation and confirms the arrangement.
synthesis.approach: Use shared calendar invitations with built-in accept or decline and date polling instead of reply-to-email availability requests, with a standard announcement template carrying date, time, room and an RSVP deadline so head counts come from the calendar responses.
synthesis.rationale: Most rounds are a short announcement or a request to hold or choose a date; a consistent invitation with RSVP built in cuts the manual tallying and the chasing, while organisers still pick dates and rooms.
